set-01.connection: Preserves the early-return scan from lesson 1 while adding remembered history.
Uses the same repeated-event recognition without the distance constraint.

set-02.connection: Reuses seen-value state but traverses backward to preserve final occurrences.

set-03.connection: Moves from comparing two multisets to stable intersection across many collections.

set-04.connection: Uses constant-time membership to grow only from consecutive-run boundaries.

set-05.connection: Turns repeated-event membership into an incremental distinct-count output.

set-06.connection: Retains lesson 7's fixed window while replacing its aggregate with duplicate state.
Practices the uniqueness invariant with a first-fixed-window result.

freq-01.connection: Consumes one frequency map as a target multiset rather than comparing equality.

freq-02.connection: Builds complete frequencies before a stable scan for the earliest singleton.

freq-03.connection: Computes an ordered multiset subtraction instead of returning a boolean.

freq-04.connection: Adds a second uniqueness check over the frequencies produced by lesson 4's pattern.

freq-05.connection: Stores first and last positions alongside counts to optimize a representative range.

freq-06.connection: Requires reasoning about how deleting one item changes the frequency distribution.

comp-01.connection: Derives difference partners and counts all index pairs, including the zero-gap case.

comp-02.connection: Keeps complement lookup but optimizes pair distance with deterministic ties.

comp-03.connection: Changes additive complements to XOR complements and counts every valid pair.

comp-04.connection: Looks up complementary remainder classes rather than an exact numeric complement.

comp-05.connection: Generalizes pair-sum lookup to four arrays through meet-in-the-middle frequencies.

comp-06.connection: Preserves partner lookup while adding divisibility, sign, zero, and overflow cases.

canon-01.connection: Uses a complete character-frequency profile as a stable grouping key.

canon-02.connection: Replaces exact value keys with normalized relative-offset signatures.

canon-03.connection: Builds hashable keys by reducing vector components and normalizing signs.

canon-04.connection: Traverses connected components and then canonicalizes each component's geometry.
Groups components by structural signatures rather than raw scalar frequencies.

canon-05.connection: Canonicalizes all cyclic rotations before grouping equivalent strings.

canon-06.connection: Normalizes signs and common factors before set-based numeric deduplication.

prefix-01.connection: Generalizes incremental range aggregation from adjacent windows to arbitrary queries.

prefix-02.connection: Looks up a needed earlier prefix instead of a needed earlier array value.

prefix-03.connection: Stores the earliest equal prefix-difference state to maximize a range.

prefix-04.connection: Counts equal normalized prefix remainders through a frequency map.

prefix-05.connection: Uses a two-dimensional count-difference state as the hash-map key.

prefix-06.connection: Encodes prefix parity as a bitmask and looks up nearby valid states.

sweep-01.connection: Moves incremental aggregation from adjacent windows to many range-update boundaries.

sweep-02.connection: Uses weighted pickup and drop-off events with explicit same-stop ordering.

sweep-03.connection: Counts threshold coverage over sparse integer intervals rather than peak rooms.

sweep-04.connection: Returns every peak interval instead of only the maximum concurrent count.

sweep-05.connection: Adds workload weights, bigint coordinates, and earliest strict overload detection.

sweep-06.connection: Computes union length under half-open semantics rather than returning merged windows.

index-01.connection: Reuses in-place mutation but encodes presence through value-index correspondence.

index-02.connection: Uses the array itself to identify one duplicate and one missing permutation value.

index-03.connection: Generalizes in-place placement to arbitrary signed input under constant-space limits.

index-04.connection: Treats permutation assignments as disjoint cycles whose sizes determine swap count.

index-05.connection: Uses array values as next pointers and locates the cycle entry to find a duplicate.

index-06.connection: Adds cycle entry, length, prefix length, and an acyclic exit sentinel.

twoptr-01.connection: Uses opposing pointers on sorted data rather than a read and write boundary.

twoptr-02.connection: Starts from nested tuple enumeration and reduces one dimension after sorting.
Uses two-pointer movement plus duplicate skipping for unique triples.

twoptr-03.connection: Maintains a variable window whose positive sum makes boundary movement monotonic.

twoptr-04.connection: Changes the window budget from distinct kinds to a count of tolerated failures.

twoptr-05.connection: Coordinates two ordered inputs while advancing only the side that cannot match.
Adds stable deduplication to a same-direction two-pointer scan.

twoptr-06.connection: Uses a dominance proof to decide which opposing pointer can safely move.

stack-01.connection: Uses stack order to retain unresolved indices rather than unmatched delimiters.

stack-02.connection: Stores unresolved indices so one warmer value can settle multiple earlier days.

stack-03.connection: Uses monotonic stack boundaries to finalize candidate rectangle widths.

stack-04.connection: Turns stack discipline into a greedy lexicographic construction.

stack-05.connection: Keeps lesson 7's fixed windows but maintains their maxima incrementally.
Generalizes LIFO storage to a monotonic double-ended queue.

stack-06.connection: Uses the stack as the only frontier where new directional conflicts can occur.

linked-01.connection: Practices preserving next references while rewiring supplied linked-list nodes.

linked-02.connection: Coordinates two list traversals but compares node identity instead of sorted values.

linked-03.connection: Uses a sentinel and a fixed pointer gap for one-pass structural removal.

linked-04.connection: Combines middle detection, reversal, and in-place weaving of one chain.

linked-05.connection: Uses fast and slow pointers before reversing and restoring half of the chain.
Requires careful node reuse and restoration of the original structure.

linked-06.connection: Moves from reusing supplied nodes to cloning a linked structure with extra references.

binary-01.connection: Preserves logarithmic lookup while determining which rotated half remains sorted.

binary-02.connection: Runs boundary search twice to locate the complete duplicate range.

binary-03.connection: Searches the minimum feasible capacity using a monotonic simulation predicate.

binary-04.connection: Changes minimum-true search into maximum-true search over feasible spacing.

binary-05.connection: Maps one logarithmic search interval onto row and column coordinates.

binary-06.connection: Searches for a valid partition boundary across two ordered arrays.

recur-01.connection: Prunes the subset decision tree to branches that choose exactly k items.

recur-02.connection: Changes include-or-skip branches into choosing each unused item for the next position.

recur-03.connection: Explores a variable-width cartesian-product decision tree.

recur-04.connection: Requires choose, recurse, and restore behavior for temporary grid visits.
Uses grid-neighbor traversal but with path-local rather than global visited state.

recur-05.connection: Adds aggressive constraint pruning to a row-by-row placement tree.

recur-06.connection: Backtracks over bounded partition lengths with syntax-based pruning.

tree-01.connection: Carries ancestor value bounds through the same recursive tree structure.

tree-02.connection: Uses postorder returns to combine evidence from two child subtrees.

tree-03.connection: Backtracks path state during a depth-first hierarchy traversal.
Looks up complementary prefix sums along the active ancestor path.

tree-04.connection: Selects one deterministic value from each breadth-first level.

tree-05.connection: Computes subtree heights while updating a path optimum that may exclude the root.

tree-06.connection: Builds recursive left and right subproblems from traversal boundaries.

heap-01.connection: Balances two priority queues to maintain a changing middle order statistic.

heap-02.connection: Keeps only the next candidate from each stream in a priority queue.
Generalizes two sorted inputs to k ordered streams.

heap-03.connection: Maintains separate priority orders for available and busy workers.
Tracks resource lifetimes while selecting a deterministic reusable worker.

heap-04.connection: Retains a bounded top-k set using the opposite heap direction.

heap-05.connection: Maintains the kth-highest boundary incrementally for every stream prefix.

heap-06.connection: Uses frequency priority repeatedly to construct, rather than merely select, output.
Begins with the same frequency-map representation before scheduling categories.

graph-01.connection: Moves from undirected components to directed prerequisites and topological ordering.

graph-02.connection: Adds edge prices and a transfer-count state to shortest-route reasoning.

graph-03.connection: Uses breadth-first layers to model simultaneous elapsed minutes.
Traverses grid connectivity from many starting components at once.

graph-04.connection: Uses graph traversal plus an identity map to reproduce every edge safely.

graph-05.connection: Computes transitive components with union-find instead of explicit traversal.

graph-06.connection: Replaces unweighted BFS layers with priority-ordered weighted distances.
Uses a priority queue to expand the currently cheapest unsettled route.

dp-01.connection: Changes position-based states into minimum counts for every reachable amount.

dp-02.connection: Uses two previous prefix states with validity-dependent transitions.

dp-03.connection: Starts from subsequence DP and then compresses states with ordered tails.
Uses binary search to replace the first tail that is not smaller.

dp-04.connection: Defines each prefix as reachable when a prior reachable prefix ends with a token.

dp-05.connection: Sorts intervals by finish time and proves a greedy selection rather than merging.

dp-06.connection: Uses the same two-state rolling optimization with a different transition objective.
